doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Stride left hand, philosophy and the singer story
summary: His left hand came from Fats Waller; the talk returns to loving what you play.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You must have developed quite a good left hand when you were working with just a drummer and no bass player, huh? Did you?
Well I had that going anyway.
Yeah. That’s been part of your playing.
Well that was from, when I was a kid, listening to Fats Waller. Look, he covered that thing man.
That’s a hard style, that stride.
Maybe it is, but if you love it and like it, then it’s not hard.
Well, that’s been a great philosophy: love it and like it and if you don’t like it, don’t do it.
I think I’m going to live that way from now on.
Why not, man? It’s the best way.
You’ve got to have a little stubbornness in there to see that it goes that way.
Yeah. And next time a singer looks at me like that, I’m going to remember what you did. I don’t know if I’d have the nerve to do it.
You didn’t want to work with her again anyway, right?
